content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp are crustaceans from the families Penaeidae and Pandalidae. They have a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a firm yet tender texture. Shrimp are eaten raw in dishes like sushi, as well as boiled, grilled, fried, or steamed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp can grow up to 30 cm, but most market varieties are small (5–10 cm).
More than 7 million tonnes of shrimp are harvested worldwide each year, making them one of the most popular seafood items.
Shrimp can change the color of their exoskeleton in response to environment and stress.
There are over 2 000 shrimp species, but only a few dozen are farmed commercially.
Shrimp can rapidly regenerate lost limbs.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, making them an excellent source of complete protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: They contain less than 1 g of fat per 100 g, with a good amount of omega‑3 polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and blood formation.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Shrimp supply selenium, zinc, iron, and iodine, which support immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A cup (≈140 g) of boiled shrimp contains roughly 120 kcal, suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain about 150 mg of cholesterol per 100 g, so people with high cholesterol should monitor portions.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: In certain regions shrimp may be contaminated with heavy metals or pathogens, so purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels can exacerbate gout symptoms in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Shrimp can be added to salads, pastas, rice dishes, soups, or served as appetizers—grilled, fried, or breaded. They are often paired with lemon‑garlic, butter, or soy‑based sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh shrimp should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C and used within 2 days. Frozen shrimp remain good for up to 12 months at –18 °C. Thaw frozen shrimp in the fridge, not at room temperature.
